D1.title: Advancing before alignment
D1.description: The policy continues moving forward before the screwdriver is aligned with the screw hole, deviating from the effective manipulation path.
D1.cameraHint: Compare the screwdriver tip and screw hole before and after the dip across the three views.

D2.title: Action jump at the control handoff
D2.description: When the operator briefly releases teleoperation control, the policy resumes execution. An abrupt action change at the handoff moves the robot away from its current working position.
D2.cameraHint: Compare the robot pose immediately before and after teleoperation is released.

D3.title: Tightening does not resume
D3.description: After the operator releases teleoperation control, the policy does not continue tightening the second screw.
D3.cameraHint: Follow the screwdriver after the handoff and check whether tightening resumes on the second screw.

D1.title: Repeated alignment adjustments
D1.description: While aligning the graphics card with the slot, the robot repeatedly adjusts and moves back and forth, temporarily moving away from its previous alignment. This corresponds to a decrease in estimated progress.
D1.cameraHint: Compare the card edge and slot as the robot adjusts its alignment.

D2.title: Slight collision during insertion
D2.description: The graphics card is not accurately aligned with the slot, causing a slight collision during insertion. This corresponds to a brief drop in estimated progress.
D2.cameraHint: Inspect the card-to-slot alignment and the contact during the insertion attempt.

D3.title: Withdrawing to reinsert
D3.description: During human intervention, the graphics card has not been fully inserted, so the operator lifts it and inserts it again. The progress drop corresponds to the withdrawal before reinsertion: a temporary setback within the correction.
D3.cameraHint: Follow the withdrawal, lift, and subsequent reinsertion across the three views.

D1.title: Brief shake as the gripper closes
D1.description: A brief shake occurs as the gripper closes, corresponding to a small decrease in estimated progress.
D1.cameraHint: Compare the instant of gripper closure with the frames immediately before and after it.

D2.title: Adjusting the part for alignment
D2.description: While aligning the part with the four-peg fixture, the robot moves it to adjust their relative positions. This adjustment corresponds to a brief decrease in estimated progress.
D2.cameraHint: Compare the part openings and the four pegs as their relative positions change.

D3.title: Releasing and regrasping too early
D3.description: The gripper opens before assembly is complete, then grasps the part again to continue assembly. This release-and-regrasp sequence corresponds to a temporary decrease in estimated progress.
D3.cameraHint: Watch the gripper release the unfinished assembly and then grasp the part again.

D1.title: Abrupt motion during human takeover
D1.description: The operator takes over too quickly, producing an abrupt action change that corresponds to a brief decrease in estimated progress.
D1.cameraHint: Compare the motion immediately before and after human takeover.

D2.title: Action jump when teleoperation is released
D2.description: During human intervention, the operator momentarily releases teleoperation control. The policy immediately resumes with an abrupt action change, corresponding to a brief decrease in estimated progress.
D2.cameraHint: Follow the transition from teleoperation to policy execution across the three views.
